title: Separate physical schema version from the replay-recorded generation; name the integrity components
trigger: External review Major 1/2/3 + I2 addition + I9. Review verdict: add a 0.7.2 before S1-A.

major_1_replay_divergence.evidence: workflow_events._REPLAY_FIELDS line 18 is 'schema_version'; _state_from_row reads project_state.schema_version. A read-triggered 9->10 migration wrote project_state.schema_version=10 with no event, while the stream replays to 9.

measured_on_real_copies.note: the old aggregate_valid did not catch it - that is exactly the overloading I9 describes

major_1_replay_divergence.fix: physical vs workflow-state version are now separate: schema_info.schema_version is the DDL generation (written by _upgrade_schema), project_state.schema_version is the generation recorded in the event stream and is only moved by an event-carrying write. transition() converges it, so the change lands in that event's state_patch.
major_1_replay_divergence.new_gate: status_snapshot() now exposes event_replay_valid: replay_events(events) must equal replay_state(current) across every _REPLAY_FIELDS member.
major_1_replay_divergence.verified_after_fix: all three real copies: replay_diff == {} , event_replay_valid True, schema_info 9->10, project_state.schema_version 9->9, revision and event count unchanged, aggregate_valid True

major_2_second_rebase_path.evidence: transition(clear_dirty_stage=...) calls rebase_dirty_classifier_state at storage.py:3068 inside its own business transaction. It is a legitimate second rebase path and emitted no DIRTY_CLASSIFIER_REBASED event, so its receipt was recorded nowhere in the event stream.
major_2_second_rebase_path.fix: the embedded rebase receipt (rebase_id, schema_version, obligation_count, bound_by='dirty_clear_transaction') is bound into that transition's payload. Test name corrected from 'the only writer' to reflect two paths.
major_2_second_rebase_path.note: does not affect the read-path guarantee: this one runs inside a business write.

major_3_provenance_contract_too_narrow.evidence: classification_contract_sha256() hashed only schema name + dirty_classification.py bytes, while the derivation also depends on ADDITIONAL_OWNERSHIP, the frozen registry and the globstar matcher.
major_3_provenance_contract_too_narrow.fix: the contract now covers dirty_classification.py, dirty.py (the mirrored branch order), artifact_ownership.py, current_artifact_ownership.py and paper_sources.py, each name-tagged before its bytes.
major_3_provenance_contract_too_narrow.note: Q14 preserved: a provenance-only change still does not produce a new classifier identity. This was done BEFORE any real project can produce a v10 cause, as the review required.

i2_addition.gap: the monotonicity loop skipped events whose effect_hashes_after was not a dict.
i2_addition.fix: an event that carries aggregate_root_hash_after must also carry a dict effect_hashes_after, otherwise effect_domain_generation_valid=False.

i9_integrity_components.aggregate_valid: the conjunction of the three; the components remain individually readable

tests_changed_beyond_additions.tests/test_factory_state_store.py: 3 tests asserted state.schema_version == SCHEMA_VERSION after a read-triggered migration. They now assert the physical version (_physical_schema_version helper) and the unchanged replay-recorded generation, which is the 0.7.2 semantics.
tests_changed_beyond_additions.tests/test_dirty_cause_classification.py: _rewind_to_v9 is now replay-aware: a faithful v9 fixture must also record 9 in the events' state_patch and recompute state_hash_after, otherwise the fixture itself violates the new replay gate.

open_items: True binary/code-version downgrade regression still pending (run bde49712's code against a schema-10 fixture).
I8: a read-only v9 precondition validator is not yet implemented; a 'schema_info=9 but incomplete' database would still be promoted to 10 by the DDL migration.
I8: read-only migration/domain drift audit across the 6 state DBs still pending.
I9: UI/doc consumers still read aggregate_valid; they should migrate to the three named components.
Review also asks for S6 item 10 (durable bounded-run contract identity) -- planned, not implemented.
